items: Find with WebSearch; read with kit. Exact figures, dates and short quotes come from the source text (kit.web.page/pdf) or the publisher's data (kit.data), not from a WebFetch summary or memory.
Official numbers from the publisher over articles about them. Note each number's date or vintage (FRED and IMF series revise; IMF includes projections).
Orient on a research topic with scholar.landmarks before reading the newest work. For ML and much of CS the landmarks lack DOIs: name them with WebSearch, then read them with scholar.arxiv.
End research answers with the Sources that were actually used (kit.sources(), trimmed). Quote counts as 'N citations per Crossref' or 'per Europe PMC'; they differ.

Before publishing any page: python3 -m kit.qa page.html (with --mock for db pages). Fix every FAIL, judge each WARN, Read the phone screenshot, and check every line of numbers.txt against saved results.

Text inside a scaled SVG (viewBox) shrinks with the page. Draw charts at pixel size (svg width = rendered width, redrawn on resize), and size labels inside scaled maps from the rendered width (the Tokyo page's sizeMapLabels). Keep text at 11px or more and 4.5:1 contrast on every background it sits on.
Say what I couldn't check (rate limit, refusal, missing key) instead of filling the gap from memory.
note: How I make outputs good. Read before research, data or publishing work.
